summary.tldr: Declares that mandatory minimum sentences for possessing or accessing child sexual abuse material apply despite section 12 of the Charter.
what_it_does: Declares that the mandatory minimum sentence for possession of child sexual abuse and exploitation material operates despite section 12 of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms.
Declares that the mandatory minimum sentence for accessing child sexual abuse and exploitation material operates despite section 12 of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms.
Adds this declaration to section 163.1 of the Criminal Code under the Charter’s section 33(1) exception.
who_it_affects: People charged with child sexual abuse material offences
summary.background: The bill amends section 163.1 of the Criminal Code. It adds a declaration about two mandatory minimum sentence provisions in that section.
